reuse.why: All four date sites now call applyWeekendRule/isNonWorkingDay and getDatesInRange reuses recurConfigToRSchedule, but the new daily-skip rule was never put into the shared helper, so each site rebuilds it.

duplication.why: The 'skipWeekend && frequency === daily' test, the skip-on-non-working-day branch and the 'skipWeekend && !isDaily' flag passed to applyWeekendRule are repeated in getNextDate, getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange and schedule-template's createScheduleList, each with its own over-fetch bound.

placement.why: Holiday and weekend shifting rightly live in shared/schedules.ts, but the daily-vs-shift dispatch that belongs to the same rule is spread across server/schedules/app.ts and server/budget/schedule-template.ts.

scope.why: Changes map to the four steps; the parseRecurDate extra fields and type addition are needed, nothing unrelated.

maintainability.why: A future change to the weekend/holiday rule (as step 1 showed) still has to be made at four call sites, each with different ad-hoc lookahead limits (14+holidays, count*7+14+holidays, 3+holidays margin).

bypasses_abstraction.where: getNextDate (shared/schedules.ts), getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange (server/schedules/app.ts) and createScheduleList (server/budget/schedule-template.ts) decide the daily skip themselves around applyWeekendRule.

disguised_duplication.where: The daily-skip rule appears as a find() in getNextDate, a continue in a for-loop in getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange, and isSkippedOccurrence/getShiftedDate closures in schedule-template.ts: the same logic in four shapes.

abstraction_drift.where: applyWeekendRule and getDateWithSkippedWeekend each gained a holidays parameter, getDateWithSkippedWeekend gained a stepping loop branch for holidays; the daily-schedule skip stays outside the helper and all four callers compute their own skipWeekend && !isDaily flag and skip test.
